issues.legal_issue: Time may be the essence of a contract for the sale of immovable property when the agreement and surrounding circumstances show that the parties intended the specified payment deadline to be fundamental.
material_facts: The agreement concerned the sale of immovable property and required a substantial part of the price to be paid within ten days.
The agreement used the word “only” both to qualify the payment amount and to qualify the ten-day period.
The vendor’s obligations to redeem the mortgage and obtain the income-tax clearance arose after payment of that sum.
The buyer did not make the payment by the deadline and sought to make it conditional on delivery of possession and completion of other obligations.
issues.conclusion: Although time is not ordinarily presumed to be of the essence in a sale of immovable property, the parties intended the payment deadline to be essential under this agreement.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 55 of the Contract Act, a failure to perform by a specified time makes the contract voidable only if the parties intended time to be of the essence. In sales of immovable property, the usual presumption is that time is not essential; that presumption may be displaced by unequivocal language or by the contract’s terms, the nature of the property, and surrounding circumstances. The Court relied on Gomathinayagam Pillai v. Pallaniswami Nadar, Govind Prasad Chaturvedi v. Hari Dutt Shastri, Hind Construction Contractors v. State of Maharashtra, Indira Kaur v. Sheo Lal Kapoor, and Jamshed Khodaram Irani v. Burjorji Dhunjibhai.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and contract_for_sale_of_immovable_property and substantial_payment_due_within_fixed_period and contract_language_emphasizes_payment_period and vendor_obligations_follow_payment

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A party brought a proceeding seeking specific performance of an agreement.
predicates.contract_for_sale_of_immovable_property: The agreement was for the sale of immovable property.
predicates.substantial_payment_due_within_fixed_per: The agreement required a substantial part of the price to be paid within a specified period.
predicates.contract_language_emphasizes_payment_per: The agreement’s wording treated the specified payment period as a distinct and emphasized term.
predicates.vendor_obligations_follow_payment: The agreement made the vendor’s relevant clearance or redemption obligations arise after the specified payment.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance proceeding concerns an immovable-property sale and the agreement emphasizes a fixed period for substantial payment before the vendor’s relevant obligations arise, the rule treats time as essential.

issues.legal_issue: A buyer is not ready and willing to perform an agreement for specific performance when the buyer fails to make the required payment and makes payment conditional on performance of terms not required by the agreement.
material_facts: The buyer did not pay the required sum within the contractual period.
After the seller notified the buyer that payment was due, the buyer did not pay the sum.
The buyer’s notices and evidence showed that payment was being withheld until possession and other requirements were provided or completed.
The agreement did not make those requirements conditions precedent to that payment.
issues.conclusion: The buyer was not ready and willing to perform the contract and was not entitled to specific performance.
issues.legal_principle: Readiness and willingness are assessed from the party’s conduct and the notices exchanged, not merely from an assertion that funds are available. A buyer who withholds a payment due under the agreement while insisting on an unsupported countercondition is not ready and willing to perform. The Court considered Nathulal v. Phoolchand but held that it did not apply to these facts.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and buyer_failed_to_make_required_payment and seller_notified_buyer_payment_was_due and buyer_conditioned_payment_on_uncontracted_requirements

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A party brought a proceeding seeking specific performance of an agreement.
predicates.buyer_failed_to_make_required_payment: The buyer did not make a payment required by the agreement.
predicates.seller_notified_buyer_payment_was_due: The seller informed the buyer that the required payment had not been made and was due.
predicates.buyer_conditioned_payment_on_uncontracte: The buyer made payment dependent on the seller first satisfying requirements that the agreement did not make conditions to payment.

issues.definition: When a buyer seeking specific performance does not make a required payment after being told it is due and conditions payment on requirements outside the agreement, the rule treats the buyer as not ready and willing.
